task.title: Money Flow Wedge Scout
task.objective: Discover the strongest tiny programmable software/AI intervention inside an existing large private-sector money flow, continuously rank a best surviving hypothesis, attack it when all build gates appear satisfied, and persist every run so future runs continue from accumulated evidence rather than restarting.

operating_protocol.discovery_floor: Every run must return at least one best surviving hypothesis even if some gates remain uncertain.
freeze_build_threshold: recurring measurable leakage or unrealized value
credible tiny fee stronger than obvious self-serve or flat-fee alternatives
no need to own the core transaction or request path
no dominant or sufficiently close incumbent or first-party feature
operating_protocol.search_behavior: Before threshold maintain a current leader and try to beat it. At threshold enter ATTACK and search for disconfirming evidence. If it survives, freeze and build; if it fails, record fatal flaw and promote the next candidate.
operating_protocol.persistence_rule: Every scheduled or manual run must append its normalized result, candidate scores, gate changes, evidence, rejected reasons, current leader and next research test to Taskman persistence before completion.

conversation_history.summary: Opportunity search narrowed away from tenders, jobs, freelance lead hunting, buyer/seller matchmaking, manufacturer sourcing and generic demand creation toward programmable interventions in existing private money flows.
Adopted eight strict build gates and lifecycle SEARCH -> ATTACK -> FROZEN-BUILD.
Rejected after attack because trigger was customer-created, intervention sat on the request path, first-party cheaper lanes and gateways existed, and performance pricing was weak.
Added two-level standard: every run must return a best surviving hypothesis while final build threshold stays strict; search breadth widened and now drills flow -> state transition -> micro-decision.
Clean authorization/fulfillment/expiry trigger, later weakened by first-party capture/reauthorization features and payment orchestration.
Strong minimum-spend shortfall economics, later weakened by cloud commitment managers and procurement/SaaS allocation tooling.
Excellent economics but current systems reconcile volume commitments, deficiency payments and make-up rights.
Promising pattern: two legitimate future uses already exist and a contractual or quota state changes which is economically optimal; detect before the decision and redirect existing activity.
Prepaid messaging credits plus scheduled sends created a good trigger; later search found mature multi-provider SMS routing/cost optimization layers.
GitHub/Taskman selected as permanent anchor for search state, evidence, rejected paths, scores, task results and conversation-derived knowledge.
Every recurring research run must read Taskman first and persist the full normalized result back to Taskman before completion.
Included/prepaid SaaS or API capacity approaching a reset with deferrable work remains a strong mechanism, but a cleaner synthetic-monitor vertical was later identified.

Provider-native app-store grace windows create a real net-margin choice for high-variable-cost apps, but the decision is app-wide/infrequent, relatively spreadsheetable and difficult to attribute for performance pricing.
Refund-promise to settlement matching remains attractive, but enterprise reconciliation products already surface missing refunds and aggregate leakage remains unquantified.
Exact tools already identify unused labels and automate carrier refunds/voids.

conversation_history.candidate: Prior-authorization expiry before scheduled service watchdog
conversation_history.summary: Current authorization tools already track expiry and flag authorizations that will expire before scheduled procedures.
Material idle-cash loss exists but treasury/bank-fee tools and bank sweeps already optimize the exact state.
Dedicated software already tracks refundable core deposits, deadlines, returns and credits.
Corporate travel software already auto-cancels to avoid no-show fees and lost value.

conversation_history.candidate: Vendor credit memo application before payment
conversation_history.summary: ERP/AP tools already track and apply unapplied vendor credits.
Quota-boundary opportunities are strongest when the financial unit and work unit are independently machine-readable and the action can be timing rather than routing through our infrastructure.

Synthetic monitoring exposes a direct billable event, schedules and APIs. Exact adaptive-frequency cost optimization was not found, but fresh research found Kentik already uses actual traffic to automatically adjust synthetic test locations, increasing incumbent absorption risk.

Leader survives but drops one point. Datadog pricing confirms per-run economics; Finout explicitly recommends frequency/location tuning; Kentik already auto-adjusts synthetic test locations from traffic and Datadog can review expensive test setups. Remaining whitespace is automated frequency optimization with verified spend counterfactual, not adaptive synthetic configuration broadly.

current_leader.name: Adaptive synthetic-monitor frequency optimizer
current_leader.state_transition: fixed synthetic-check schedule -> traffic/deployment/incident/risk state changes -> current cadence becomes unnecessarily expensive -> lower eligible frequency/coverage within guardrails -> preserve required detection quality -> verified billable test runs avoided
current_leader.why_survived: Synthetic runs remain explicitly usage-priced and machine-scheduled. Current systems expose frequencies, locations, traffic and incident signals, making a read-only recommendation layer feasible without touching customer traffic. Exact searches did not find a sufficiently close product whose commercial job is continuously optimizing frequency against real-time risk and then charging on verified avoided run spend. The hypothesis is weaker because Kentik already performs traffic-driven automatic synthetic configuration at the location level and observability vendors have workflow/cost automation primitives.
strongest_evidence: Datadog currently prices browser synthetics from $12 per 1,000 runs and API synthetics from $5 per 10,000 runs, so frequency is directly monetized.
Finout explicitly identifies check-frequency and test-location tuning as Datadog synthetic cost-optimization levers.
Kentik states that actual traffic can automatically configure/maintain synthetic tests and adjust test locations when traffic flows change.

Site24x7 describes intelligent test scheduling based on historical/predictive data as a way to reduce synthetic costs while preserving coverage, supporting technical plausibility but also future incumbent absorption risk.
current_leader.closest_threat: Kentik already auto-adjusts synthetic locations from observed traffic; Datadog provides expensive-test setup review, workflow automation and cost-optimization primitives. The wedge dies if first-party systems also mutate frequency automatically or if dynamic savings beyond one-time manual tuning are small.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read synthetic definitions, historical runs, traffic, deploy/incident state and SLO constraints; compute minimum-safe frequency; recommend changes first and optionally write schedules later. Maintain a baseline-versus-optimized run ledger and block changes that violate detection-latency/SLO policy.
current_leader.monetization: Per optimized monitor-month or capped share of verified avoided synthetic-run spend while reliability guardrails remain satisfied.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Dynamic optimization may add little beyond one-time static tuning, and adaptive synthetic configuration is close enough to existing vendor capabilities that incumbent absorption risk is now material.
current_leader.next_research_test: Find evidence of real enterprise synthetic estates and billing pain, quantify dynamic-versus-static savings using realistic run-count distributions, and inspect Datadog/New Relic/Kentik/Checkly for automatic frequency mutation. Kill if dynamic incremental savings are small or first-party adaptive frequency already exists.

runner_ups.reason: General mechanism remains structurally strong but still lacks a better specific vertical than synthetics.
Excellent attribution but unquantified leakage and closer reconciliation competition.
Real economics but infrequent app-wide control and weaker performance attribution.

new_search_rules: Exact adaptive frequency remains distinct from traffic-driven adaptive test-location selection, but the latter materially raises incumbent absorption risk.
A direct per-run price is not sufficient; prove incremental savings beyond a one-time static best-practice tuning exercise.
For observability wedges, compare against first-party workflow automation primitives, not only explicit named cost-optimization features.
When a vendor already uses traffic to mutate one synthetic configuration dimension automatically, penalize adjacent dimensions even if the exact proposed feature is absent.
